title: Tuning the Reversible E – Z Photoisomerization of a Stilbene-like Ligand via Lanthanide Complexation
abstract: The segmental stilbene-like ligand E- DiL1 displays only an irreversible E → Z photoisomerization under UV-light irradiation due to the overlapping of its absorption spectrum with that of its isomer Z-DiL1, which is further hampered by competing prejudicial intra/intermolecular photoreactions. These limitations can be overcome by exploiting the conformational and electronic changes induced upon connecting E-DiL1 to [Y(hfac)3] rare earth cargoes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Cryptic Cytochrome P450 Radical Cyclase Catalyzes Naphthalene-Ring Closure in Rifamycin Biosynthesis
abstract: The enzymatic assembly of the 8-hydroxynaphthalene chromophore in rifamycins presents a classic biosynthetic paradox: the off-PKS precursor, prorifamycin A (1a), readily suffers nonenzymatic deoxygenative collapse in solution into the aberrant product 8-deoxynaphthoquinones. Here, using in cellulo genetic manipulation, stepwise pathway reconstitution, in vitro enzymatic assays, molecular docking, and DFT calculations, we identified Rif-Orf0 to be a cytochrome P450 radical cyclase.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: EnsemblePAE: A PAE-Guided Structure-Based Model for Efficient Sampling of Protein Conformational Ensembles from AlphaFold Predictions
abstract: AlphaFold has revolutionized protein structure prediction, yet extracting conformational dynamics from a single predicted structure remains a major challenge. Here, we present EnsemblePAE, a PAE-guided structure-based model that transforms AlphaFold’s predicted aligned error (PAE) into heterogeneous native interactions for efficient coarse-grained simulations. By systematically evaluating different PAE rescaling schemes, we identify an optimal formulation that balances structural stability and conformational flexibility.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Linking Solvation Structure, Activity, and Electronic Structure to Electrochemical Stability in Lithium-ion Battery Electrolytes
abstract: Electrolyte stability governs the performance and lifetime of Li-ion batteries, yet a quantitative molecular-level understanding of how salt concentration influences electrochemical stability remains elusive. Here, we combine molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, a lattice fluid theory, X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS), density functional theory (DFT), and electrochemical measurements to quantitatively link solvation structure, thermodynamic activity, and electronic structure to the electrochemical stability of LiPF6 in EC/EMC (3:7 v/v) across a wide concentration range. We derive simple analytic expressions for species activities, parametrized using coordination numbers obtained from Raman spectroscopy, and validated against both MD simulations and experiment. Increasing salt concentration promotes PF6– participation in the Li+ solvation shell while suppressing free solvent populations, leading to systematic changes in the activities of species and an expanded electrochemical stability window. The lattice fluid theory directly links concentration-dependent solvation structure to measurable shifts in redox potentials via the Nernst equation, in good agreement with both computational predictions and experimental observations. DFT-predicted shifts in the unoccupied electronic states are confirmed by XAS measurements. These results establish a quantitative framework linking solvation structure, thermodynamic activity, and electronic structure to electrolyte stability, enabling the rational design of electrolytes with tailored electrochemical stability windows.

title: Water-Soluble Pd12 Multicomponent Cage Enables Selective Separation of 1,4-Dibromonaphthalene from 1,5-Dibromonaphthalene and Regioselective Bromination of Naphthalene
abstract: The synthesis of intricate supramolecular architectures is driven by the desire to translate structural complexity into functional specificity. Herein, we report the formation of an unusual M12L4L′4 cage (MCC) with double-walled knotted architecture via multicomponent self-assembly of a tripyridyl ligand (L), a tricarboxylate ligand (L′), and a cis-Pd(II) acceptor (M). The structure of the MCC resembles a truncated tetrahedron with two overlaid walls enclosing a distorted cavity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Photoaffinity Capture of Unit-Resolved Ubiquitin–Decoder Contacts Underlying Topology-Selective Recognition of Heterotypic Chains
abstract: Heterotypic K63/K48 polyubiquitin chains encode diverse cellular outcomes, ranging from proteasomal degradation to nonproteolytic signaling. Although chain topology is increasingly recognized as a critical determinant of these functions, how architectures composed of the same linkage types are decoded into distinct outputs remains poorly understood. This gap has persisted because molecular technologies capable of both chemically capturing topology-selective decoders and defining the unit-resolved contacts underlying selective recognition remain undeveloped.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Cascade Synthesis of Alternating Thiolactone–Episulfide Copolymers via Multi-Site Single-Unit Monomer Insertion
abstract: Alternating copolymers are fundamental sequence-controlled polymers, but their synthesis from two independently polymerizable monomers remains challenging because conventional methods rely on selective cross-propagation, limiting monomer combinations and structural diversity. Here, we report a two-step cascade strategy that decouples sequence control from direct alternating copolymerization. We target thiolactones and episulfides, important sulfur-containing heterocycles accessible from biobased or low-cost feedstocks.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
